newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-World nickel output to rise 3.6 pct/yr -ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-World nickel output to rise 3.6 pct/yr -ABARE.

text.p: World nickel production is projected to grow by 3.6 percent annually to the year 2002 when production will total 1.9 million tonnes, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.
Higher production in 1997 is forecast to come largely from existing producers operating at higher capacity levels, ABARE said.
World nickel consumption is projected to increase to 1.13 million tonnes in the year 2002 from 956,000 tonnes in 1996.
The increase in consumption is being underpinned by stronger demand for nickel from stainless steel producers, ABARE said.
Nickel consumption is expected to exceed production during 1997 and into 1998.
"Consequently the LME (London Metal Exchange) nickel price is forcast to increase during this period, averaging US$8,025 a tonne in 1997 and US$9,000 a tonne in 1998," ABARE said.
From late 1998 prices will come under downward pressure from newer low cost nickel making operations, ABARE said.
Australian nickel mine production is projected to increase by 75 percent or 89,000 tonnes to 207,000 tonnes in 2001/02 (July/June).
Refined nickel production is forecast to rise by 69 percent or 46,000 tonnes to 113,000 tonnes over the same period, ABARE said.
